questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

A new book on games will be released by the publishers next week.
options_en: The publishers will release a new book on games next week.
The publishers will publish a new book on games next week.
The publishers will be releasing a new book next week.
The publishers would release a new book next week.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Future Indefinite. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Future Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object.

For example:

The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): The publishers will release a new book on games next week.

Q. Of the past

R. The great filmmakers

S. Films are clearly borrowed from
questions.solution_en:

Part Q then qualifies the time period or era from which these great filmmakers are from, indicating they are historical figures. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: The cinematic effects in her films are clearly borrowed from the great filmmakers of the past.

Directions [Set of 4 Questions]:Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

Jenna had just moved into a new apartment in the heart of the city. She had spent the entire day unpacking and arranging her stuff in her new home. She was exhausted, so she decided to take a break and explore the neighbourhood. She wandered down the bustling streets, taking in the sights and sounds of the city. As she was walking, she noticed an antique shop tucked away in a quiet alley. Curiosity got the best of her, and she decided to go in and take a look around. The shop was filled with all sorts of unique items, but one caught Jenna's eye - an ornate key with intricate designs etched into it. Jenna knew she had to have it. She purchased the key and brought it back to her apartment. She tried it in every lock in her new home, but none of them seemed to fit. Frustrated, she put the key down and went to bed. The next morning, Jenna woke up to find that the key was missing. She searched high and low, but it was nowhere to be found. She retraced her steps from the previous day, but no one had seen it. Days turned into weeks, and Jenna was starting to lose hope of ever finding the key again. That is until she received a package in the mail. Inside was a note that read, "I found your key. Meet me at the antique shop where you purchased it." Jenna rushed to the antique shop, and there she found an elderly man waiting for her. He handed her the key and explained that it had been passed down through generations of his family. He wanted her to have it, as he believed she was meant to find it. Jenna was overwhelmed with gratitude and felt a sense of belonging in her new home. The key may have been lost for a time, but it ultimately led her to a meaningful connection with the past.

questions.q_en: What is a phrasal verb?
options_en: A group of words that has a deducible meaning
A small group of words standing together as a conceptual unit
An idiomatic phrase consisting of a verb and another element
A sentence with a blank to fill with a phrase
questions.solution_en:
An idiomatic phrase consisting of a verb and another element, typically either an adverb, as in break down, or a preposition, for example see to, or a combination of both, such as look down on.

Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined word segment in the given sentence.

A swarm of bees swam gracefully through the clear waters, moving in perfect synchrony.
questions.solution_en:
The most appropriate option to substitute the underlined word segment in the given sentence is: option (b) "School of fish". The original sentence describes something swimming through the water, and "school of fish" is the correct term to refer to a group of fish swimming together in synchrony. A 'swarm of bees' is a group of honey bees that leave their hive to establish a new colony which isn't apt to use in the context of swimming.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

Option (a): This refers to a group of crows, but crows do not swim, so it doesn't fit the context.

Option (c): A herd refers to a group of cattle, but they don't swim in the same way fish do.

Option (d): A grove refers to a group of trees, which is unrelated to the action of swimming.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

She asked, "Are you meeting my partners next week?"
options_en: She asked about our meeting her partners next week.
She asked if we meet her partners next week.
She asked if we were meeting her partners the following week.
She asked if we were meeting her partners next week.
questions.solution_en:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "said" in Direct Speech is changed into "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc.

In Indirect speech, the verb is always placed after the subject, unlike in Direct Speech.

If there is a question in the Direct Speech whose answer can come as "Yes" or "No" in the Indirect Speech, we should use the conjunctions "if" or "whether".

For example:

Ravi said to me, "Is she studying?" (Direct Speech)

Ravi asked me if she was studying. (Indirect Speech)

Also, the sentence in the Direct Speech is in the Present continuous tense. So, the tense in the Indirect Speech should be in the Past continuous tense.

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'If' will be introduced in the sentence.

'Are you' will be changed to 'we were'.

'My' will be changed to 'her'.

'Next week' will be changed to 'following week'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (c): She asked if we were meeting her partners the following week.

questions.q_en:
Directions [Set of 5 Questions]: Directions: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The population of Venice, more than 170,000 after the second world war, has ____________(A) steadily to some 52,000 today. Remaining residents still feel _______________(B) to live in a city of such beauty, many believing their culture survives despite the onslaught, but they also grieve at the losses, lose heart, and move away at a rate of 1,000 a year to homes on the mainland. A Venice without Venetians - without significant numbers of permanent residents - is ______________(C) for as early as 2030. It is no ________________(D) to say that mass tourism - adding to Venice's existing issues with mismanagement of the environment, corruption, political stasis and now the climate emergency - is bringing the community, the lagoon, and a fabulous heritage to within a ___________(E) of collapse.

Which of the following can fit in the blank D?
questions.solution_en: The given blank will take the word 'exaggeration' which means 'a statement that represents something as better or worse than it really is' as the sentence says that the excessive tourism in Venice has affected it adversely in many different ways and this is not an overstatement. 'Logic', 'unfolding' (means 'developing or becoming clear to other people') and 'appetite' (means 'a strong desire or liking for something') do not fit contextually in the given sentence. Hence, the answer is option d).
